prerequisites: Basic knowledge of mechanics at a degree level in industrial engineering (Theory of Machines and Mechanisms).
Basic knowledge of different machine elements, their proper selection and calculation (can be acquired simultaneously).

learning_outcomes.text: Apply the acquired knowledge and problem-solving ability in new or unfamiliar environments within broader or multidisciplinary contexts related to Mechanics.

Integrate such knowledge and confront the complexity of formulating judgments based on incomplete or limited information, including reflections on the responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
Communicate conclusions (as well as the knowledge and underlying reasons that support them) to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Possess learning skills that allow for continued self-directed or autonomous study.
Organize conceptual design activity to support decision-making and selection among possible solutions to an engineering problem.
Develop skills for working in cooperative and multidisciplinary technical teams.
Plan the assembly, commissioning, and maintenance of a mechatronic equipment or system.
Discriminate the most critical components in a mechatronic system and justify their possible redesign from the control system's point of view.
Acquire knowledge, techniques, and skills that represent an increase in research and innovation potential and promote technology transfer to industry.

Students will be able to approach the overall design of a machine, starting from a solid model, which will then allow them to create virtual models, simulations, and calculations, as well as manufacturing drawings and bills of materials for the different subassemblies.
Students will be able to manage design changes throughout its development period, documented.

syllabus_topics: Mechanical systems applied in mechatronic systems
teaching_methods: Classroom practices (problem-solving assisted by the professor)
Laboratory practices (learning and using mechanical design and simulation software)
assessment_rules: The final grade is based on a final project (50%), practical assignments and reports (40%), and active classroom participation (10%). The final project includes a technical report submitted at least one week before the evaluation session, followed by an oral defense. Practical assignments consist of deliverables from individual and group work throughout the semester. Active participation is assessed by the professor during practical classroom and laboratory sessions. For the extraordinary examination, evaluation will be based solely on a final project (100%), requiring a technical report submission at least one week prior and an oral defense. Students must request the final project statement and instructions at least two months in advance for the extraordinary examination.
